newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkish Germans a key advertising target group-IP.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Germans a key advertising target group-IP.

text.p: Turks living in Germany have emerged as a key target group for television advertisers, media marketing company IP Deutschland said on Tuesday.
Ninety-seven percent of Turkish Germans watch television several times a week, compared with 91 percent of ethnic Germans the company said.
"The data impressively confirm the importance of Turkish Germans as a vital consumer group for the advertising industry," IP said in a statement.
The company said it had also observed little difference in buying power between the two groups in its research.
"There is hardly a difference between Turks and Germans in terms of employment," the company said. "In both groups, just over 50 percent (of the total populations) have a job.
"A third of Turkish households have a net household monthly income of 4,000 marks or more, compared with 40 percent among Germans," IP said.
Of about seven million foreigners living in Germany, people of Turkish descent represent the largest group with a population of 2.4 million, IP said.
Among ethnic Turks, 82 percent fall within the important demographic group of 14-49 year olds, the company added.
IP sells advertising time for the Turkish-language television station TRT.

Advertising agency Springer & Jacoby, which represents luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz, told news magazine Der Spiegel this week that they planned to expand their advertising for the car in Turkish-language newspapers and on TRT.
